title: Standard of Living
summary: Needs and wants, standard of living and quality of life, how it is measured, causes and effects of poverty and unemployment, and how government and communities improve living standards.

notes.text: Needs, wants and standard of living

items: **Needs**: things we must have to survive: food, water, shelter, clothing, healthcare.
**Wants**: things we would like to have but can live without: a cellphone upgrade, branded shoes, a holiday.

notes.text: The level of wealth, goods and services available to a person or community, for example income, housing, food and access to services.
A broader idea of well-being, including health, safety, education, freedom, a clean environment and good relationships, not only money.

headers: A higher standard of living shows…
rows: Clean water, electricity, sanitation, schools and clinics
Formal houses with services rather than informal shelters
Higher life expectancy, lower infant mortality
Higher literacy rates and more years of schooling

notes.text: A situation in which people do not have enough income or resources to meet their basic needs.

items: **Absolute poverty**: people cannot afford even the basic needs for survival.
**Relative poverty**: people are poor compared with others in their society.

rows: Low levels of education and skills
Inequality and the legacy of apartheid
Crime and substance abuse may increase
Living in informal settlements without services

notes.text: When people who are able and willing to work cannot find a job.

notes.title: Calculating the unemployment rate
notes.problem: A town has a labour force of 50 000 people, of whom 16 000 are unemployed. Calculate the unemployment rate.

items: **Government**: social grants, free basic services, RDP houses, no-fee schools, free primary healthcare, public works jobs.
**Businesses**: creating jobs, training workers, corporate social investment.
**Communities**: food gardens, stokvels, NGOs and volunteers.
**Individuals**: staying in school, gaining skills, starting small businesses, budgeting wisely.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Taxes paid by working people and businesses fund the services and grants that improve the standard of living for everyone. This is called **redistribution of income**.
